questions.q: What does this course assume you already know coming in?
options: SQL — joins, CTEs, indexes, primary/foreign keys, and fact/dimension tables — from T-SQL Development or equivalent experience
Nothing at all — it starts SQL from zero
Python and Spark programming
A different cloud data warehouse product
questions.explain: This is a focused specialization, not a mega-course — it builds directly on SQL knowledge you already have rather than re-teaching it.

options: Snowflake's web-based interface, where you write SQL, browse databases, and select a role and warehouse
A separate desktop application unrelated to Snowflake
A command-line-only tool with no visual interface
A Power BI feature for connecting to any database
questions.explain: Snowsight is Snowflake's web interface — worksheets, the database object tree, and role/warehouse selectors all live there.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what stands out immediately about a Snowflake query compared to SSMS?
options: The role and warehouse powering the query are both explicit and switchable right in the worksheet, not buried in settings
Snowflake queries cannot use SELECT statements
There is no way to see which database you're connected to
Snowflake has no concept of roles at all
questions.explain: Snowflake makes both 'who's asking' (role) and 'what's paying for compute' (warehouse) explicit and visible per query, unlike SSMS's more implicit connection model.

questions.q: What are the four groups this course moves through?
options: Foundations & SQL differences; getting data in & shaping it; running it like production; connecting it & closing out
Only SQL syntax lessons repeated four times
Four unrelated database platforms
Four separate certification exams
questions.explain: The course is organized into these four groups, moving from fundamentals through data loading/transformation, production practices, and finally integration and the capstone.

questions.q: What is the Chapter 15 capstone project, according to this lesson?
options: A real pipeline: raw data loaded into Snowflake, transformed and modeled, secured with RBAC, and connected to Power BI
A multiple-choice-only final exam with no hands-on work
A repeat of Chapter 1's lab with no new content
An assignment unrelated to anything covered earlier in the course
questions.explain: The capstone ties together loading, transformation, dimensional modeling, security, and Power BI connectivity into one real end-to-end project.
